title: Provenance is now recorded at creation, but the published asset still carries no machine-readable mark
evidence: 2026-09-21 03:5xZ: the DB half landed (42cd73d) -- photos.synthetic + photos.provenance are written at creation through ContentPillars::Photo.import_render (single choke point for both render producers) and the corpus is backfilled 337/337 with provenance.embedded=false. Closes on live evidence: a published asset whose bytes read the mark back out.

2026-09-21 session (turbo-carnival, founder): DECISION MADE -- disclose. This item is no longer waiting on Tim. Grounded in THESIS itself: pillar 2 already mandates an attribution spine (base_model/seed/prompt_hash/quality_metrics) that stops at the database and never reaches the published asset, and the existing red line 'never fake engagement, buy followers, or pay for growth' already forbids presenting synthetic as real to move the growth metric -- so the fix is the spine reaching the asset, not a new policy. Recorded two ways: (1) a new founder rail in THESIS.md -- 'Never publish a render without a machine-readable synthetic mark, or present synthetic imagery as photography'; (2) a validated OpenSpec change openspec/changes/add-synthetic-provenance (proposal + tasks + content-provenance delta, openspec validate --strict passes, 0/15 tasks). Scope: mark at creation -> embed digitalSourceType=trainedAlgorithmicMedia in the SERVED bytes -> fail-closed publish gate consistent with the NSFW/realism gates -> viewer-facing disclosure. Remaining work is implementation (additive migration, publish path, rspec) and should run through the repo's normal worker path rather than ad-hoc from a session. This item stays open until live evidence shows a published asset carrying a readable mark.

2026-09-21 03:5xZ ops-triage: PHASE 1 IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED (this run's commit). The DB half of the mark now exists and is written at creation: migration 20260921040000 adds photos.synthetic (nullable, NO default -- unknown is not human origin) + photos.provenance jsonb; ContentPillars::Photo.import_render is the single choke point both render producers call (Growth::ContentGenerator sync + Growth::RenderSalvage recovery, which each used to create the row themselves); ContentPillars::PhotoProvenance records digital_source_type=trainedAlgorithmicMedia, source, embedded=false, prompt_hash (sha256 of run.prompt) and seed/quality_metrics when the run carries them; lib/tasks/photos.rake marks the corpus (APPLY=1: marked=337 remaining_unmarked=0). Verified: 8 new rspec examples + 78 examples 0 failures across spec/services/growth and spec/models; the live write path exercised in a rolled-back transaction (in-tx photo=352 synthetic=true embedded=false run_id=476 prompt_hash=7d50e64953af, persisted=false after rollback); selftest 177 assertions 0 failures; new probe check photo-provenance-unmarked silent on live data, critical when a producer stops calling import_render, warn on unmarked rows (both branches exercised). CORRECTION to the change's premise: the attribution spine it assumes is not in the data -- pipeline_runs.variables carries only sync_producer for the growth path (10 of 457 runs carry a seed), so base_model/seed are recorded when present and omitted otherwise. REMAINS OPEN because the rail is 'never publish a render without a machine-readable synthetic mark' and the mark is still DB-only: tasks 2.x (embed digitalSourceType in the SERVED bytes) and 3.x (fail-closed publish gate) change the bytes Meta fetches and the live publish path -- routed to the worker path by the founder note, not done from a session. Closes on live evidence: a published asset whose bytes read the mark back out.
